title: Honey, I Shrunk the Kids LEGO Ideas project hits 10K votes ahead of review deadline
summary: A fan-made LEGO Ideas build inspired by the 1989 film Honey, I Shrunk the Kids has reached 10,000 supporters, just in time for the September review window.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A LEGO Ideas project based on the 1989 film Honey, I Shrunk the Kids has reached the 10,000-vote milestone, according to Brick Fanatics. Created by fan designer TangTaizong, the build recreates a memorable scene from the movie, featuring an oversized lawnmower and giant LEGO brick towering over tiny, shrunken minifigures.

The model includes five minifigures, among them the four main characters from the film - Amy, Nick, Little Russ and Ron - all built at the shrunken scale to match the movie's forced-perspective look.

Reaching 10,000 votes means the project qualifies for LEGO's official review process, alongside 85 other projects, ahead of the review window closing on 7 September 2026. This is not a confirmation that the set will be produced - LEGO still has to review and approve it before it can become an official retail set.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the main routes for fan-designed concepts to become genuine LEGO sets, following the success of previous fan projects like the Tintin Moon Rocket and Floating Sea Otters. For UK fans and collectors, a nostalgic 1980s film tie-in like this could be a popular addition if approved, especially for those who enjoy display-focused or scene-based builds.

## What to watch next
LEGO Group is expected to announce which projects from this review round have been approved after the 7 September deadline. Until then, this remains a fan project - not an officially confirmed LEGO set - so approval is not guaranteed.

Bundling desirable characters into a premium set rather than a cheaper standalone release (as LEGO did back in 2017 with the Bounty Hunter Speeder Bike Battle Pack) makes them far less accessible for fans who just want the figures, not the full model.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO Sagrada Família vs UCS Super Star Destroyer: same price, very different builds
summary: Two record-breaking LEGO sets are landing within a month of each other at an identical £649.99 price – Brick Fanatics compares the 12,060-piece Sagrada Família with the 136cm-long UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has put two of LEGO's biggest upcoming releases head-to-head: 21065 Sagrada Família and 75457 UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer. Both sets share the same price tag of £649.99 / €749.99 / $799.99, but they couldn't be more different in approach.

21065 Sagrada Família releases on 1 November and holds the record for highest piece count ever at 12,060 pieces, standing 62cm high, 47cm wide and 39cm deep. It relies heavily on small elements, including plenty of 1x1 pieces, to recreate the intricate detail of Gaudí's Barcelona landmark.

75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer releases a month earlier, on 1 October, and is officially the longest LEGO set ever made at 136cm, despite a much lower piece count of 6,130. Its scale comes from sheer horizontal length rather than density, with a 20cm height (partly from its display stand) and 50cm width.

According to the comparison, Sagrada Família is about intricate detail and piece density, while the Executor is about outright physical scale and engineering to support that huge length.

## Why it matters
For collectors weighing up a big-ticket purchase this autumn, this comparison highlights that piece count and price alone don't tell the whole story. Display space, building style preference (detailed architecture vs large-scale engineering), and shelf footprint all matter just as much as the number on the box.

## What to watch next
With both sets releasing within weeks of each other in the run-up to the holidays, expect plenty of reviews and side-by-side display comparisons once builders get their hands on them.

title: LEGO Super Mario Minifigures vs Interactive Figures: What's Changing in 2027
summary: New minifigure-style Mario sets are coming in January 2027, phasing out the theme's original interactive electronic figures. Here's how the two approaches compare.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Eight new LEGO Super Mario sets have been revealed, due to launch on 1 January 2027, and they'll feature traditional minifigures of Mario, Luigi, Peach and other Nintendo characters instead of the electronic interactive figures the theme has used since launch.

LEGO Super Mario first arrived in 2020 as a collaboration between the LEGO Group and Nintendo. Its big gimmick was an electronic Mario figure with a digital chest screen and eyes that reacted to special stickers on 2x2 tiles, playing sounds and music as you built and ran through course pieces. Interactive Luigi and Peach figures followed, alongside expansion sets, Character Packs, Power-Up Packs, a 2024 refresh of the Starter Courses, and Mario Kart-themed builds in 2025.

The upcoming 2027 wave swaps that tech-driven approach for standard minifigures, effectively retiring the interactive figure format in favour of a more traditional building experience.

## Why it matters
This is a notable shift in direction for one of LEGO's longest-running licensed themes. Fans who found the interactive electronics limited or gimmicky may welcome the change, while others who enjoyed the sound and light features may see it as a step back. It also signals that the LEGO SMART Play System, used in newer themes, may be taking over as the go-to interactive format going forward.

## What to watch next
More details on the full 2027 Super Mario line-up are expected as the January release date approaches. It's worth watching whether the LEGO Group confirms this is a full transition away from interactive figures across the theme, or just for this particular wave of sets.
